title: Ordered within-visit systolic relaxation did not improve albuminuria prediction beyond mean and variability across two NHANES samples
abstract: The direction of change across routine blood-pressure readings is lost by their mean and standard deviation. We tested first-minus-third seated systolic pressure as an additional predictor of spot urinary albumin/creatinine >=30 mg/g. A prespecified weighted ridge model included flexible age, BMI, HbA1c, serum creatinine, mean systolic/diastolic pressures and their within-visit SDs, plus sex. NHANES 2007–08 supplied 4558 discovery adults; separate 2009–10 supplied 4983 confirmation adults. Brier gain (baseline minus augmented model) was −0.0000741 in source PSU-grouped cross-validation and −0.0000156 in frozen confirmation. Target rescaled-PSU bootstrap 95% interval was −0.0000964 to +0.0000677; source/target refits gave −0.000316 to +0.000111. AUROC decreased by 0.000221. Tiny sign changes under alternative BP averaging and first-morning urine did not establish useful incremental prediction. This is a scoped negative result for a signed linear addition, not evidence of absent biological information. Independent survey samples are not external-program replication; unlinked repeat participation cannot be excluded. Author checks and a clean offline rerun are provided, not independent peer review.
